blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Changing sparse autoencoder (SAE) codes can alter both intervention direction and magnitude, so comparing intervention effects requires a strength control specifying what is held equal. Norm matching and output calibration provide different controls, but whether interventions yield different effects across codes after strength matching remains unclear. We compare intervention effects under these controls for fixed feature groups in Gemma and Llama and observe: (1) Whole-patch scaling. With one coefficient per input, full-output Kullback-Leibler (KL) calibration leaves smaller mean effect gaps from the encoder-based reference intervention than total-norm matching for nonnegative least-squares (NNLS) refits. On new Llama inputs, total-norm matching loses 11 reference transfers, whereas full-output calibration preserves every transfer decision. (2) Positionwise scaling. On a small matched gender-agreement subset, positionwise norm matching leaves smaller observed mean gaps than full-output calibration. (3) Answer exclusion. Compared with unscaled NNLS, answer-excluded calibration reduces gaps in the measured subject-verb agreement comparisons but increases them for gender refits. Full-output KL calibration also reduces larger gaps for norm-matched constructed candidates, although matching coverage is incomplete in several settings. Since calibration uses the evaluated input's outputs, it serves as a diagnostic of residual disagreement.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) represent model activations through feature
directions and sparse coefficients ( Bricken et al., 2023 ; Huben et al., 2024 ) .
The decoder supplies a dictionary of feature directions, and
the encoder assigns coefficients, collectively called a code ,
that specify their contributions to an activation’s reconstruction.
Intervening on selected
features lets researchers test their role in model behavior ( Marks et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
With one coefficient per input, full-output KL calibration leaves smaller mean NNLS gaps than
total-norm matching across five earlier cohorts, with prospective confirmation
in Llama-128K. On that new panel, total-norm matching loses encoder transfers
that full-output KL calibration preserves.
Full-output KL need not give the closest agreement: positionwise
matching does so on a descriptive 24-input gender subset. Answer exclusion
also increases gender NNLS gaps relative to the unscaled patches. Calibration also reduces larger gaps from constructed candidates,
with matching coverage dependent on the search range.

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
The experiments study model outputs on templated sentence prefixes, without
human participants or personal records. The main lexical inventory was
authored for the study and contains common nouns denoting people and roles.
It is not a representative sample of English usage or of any demographic
group. The gender materials manipulate explicit male/female cues to test
the model’s reflexive continuations. They do not operationalize gender
identity or support conclusions about fairness. Neither phenomenon is a
test of social bias or model safety.

coefficients on their respective encoder supports. The local objective
minimizes the projection of the candidate patch onto the encoder patch,

code receive no optimization restart. The construction uses geometry, not
the measured linguistic effect, as its objective.

Discovery uses the normalized-margin utility U ⁡ ( G ) U(G) in

It measures all active singleton contrasts, then forms a 64-feature shortlist

proposals are ranked by qualification, number of covered cases, worst-case

group size and then feature IDs. This rule can select a larger group after
a smaller one has already qualified.

blocks.en:
Controlled agreement tests probe whether predictions respect syntactic
structure despite distracting nouns or reduced semantic cues ( Gulordava et al., 2018 ) . BLiMP extends minimal-pair evaluation
across a wider range of grammatical phenomena ( Warstadt et al., 2020 ) . Our targeted next-token contrasts
do not provide that breadth. Studies of number-tracking units in recurrent
models ( Lakretz et al., 2019 ) and causal mediation in transformers ( Finlayson et al., 2021 ) instead investigate internal contributions
to agreement. Related intervention methods test mediation of gender bias ( Vig et al., 2020 ) or remove decodable information to assess its
behavioral role ( Elazar et al., 2021 ) . These studies motivate
distinguishing information present in a representation from information used
in a prediction. Our experiment asks the narrower question of comparability
between interventions on the same group.

blocks.en:
The indirect-object-identification circuit study evaluates a proposed circuit
using faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria ( Wang et al., 2023 ) . Automated circuit discovery searches for relevant
computational subgraphs ( Conmy et al., 2023 ) , and AtP* addresses errors
in gradient-based approximations used to localize components ( Kramár et al., 2024 ) . Distributed alignment search learns a correspondence
between proposed causal variables and neural representations ( Geiger et al., 2024 ) . We neither rediscover a circuit under each code
nor optimize a new causal alignment. The feature group and decoder stay fixed,
and the reported effects come from executed interventions, not gradient
approximations. Calibration agreement therefore does not establish that this
group is a complete or minimal mechanism.

blocks.en:
Sanity checks for saliency maps test whether explanations depend on the model
and data they purport to explain ( Adebayo et al., 2018 ) .
Explanation-robustness analyses ask how explanations change under small input
perturbations ( Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola, 2018 ) . Our varying object is the code
and resulting patch for a fixed input, rather than the input or trained model.
The common lesson is to specify what a stability test holds fixed and what it
can establish. Two interventions agreeing with each other is not an external
criterion of explanatory correctness, even when both change the target answer.

Variable importance can also vary across well-performing prediction models,
as studied through model-class reliance and variable-importance clouds ( Fisher et al., 2019 ; Dong and Rudin, 2019 ) . Our decoder instead stays fixed
while its codes vary. This connection
motivates specifying the object held fixed in a comparison, without equating
the two sources of variation.

blocks.en: H.4 Llama Confirmation: Execution Environment and Measured Cost

The new Llama-128K confirmation used one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU per

blocks.en:
Source-to-table checks on the internal archives establish agreement between
manuscript values and reviewed records. They do not independently recompute
every interval or regenerate model outputs.
The accompanying CPU supplement contains the 570 attempted NNLS

results, shared coefficients, six KL budgets and the seven search-range
continuation cells. The records include sentence prefixes and token IDs,
pair/case/block identifiers, actual matching masks, scalar measurements,
pinned asset metadata and scientific excerpts of the internal plans.
These excerpts are not externally timestamped registrations.

counts, reselects shared coefficients from recorded calibration KL values,
and checks retained scalar selections and budget intersections.
It has been tested from a clean extraction in a new Python environment
without the research archive.
